**Continuous 2.4.2**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from an earlier release, install the new `.vsix` the same way, then see **Continued is now Continuous** below.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.4.2.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md).

| Platform                    | File                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.4.2.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.4.2.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.4.2.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.4.2.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.4.2.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.4.2.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.4.2-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

The Linux armhf and Alpine packages of 2.2.0 are gone: their native modules were built for other platforms and did not work.

## Continued is now Continuous

The extension is renamed Continuous, with the ID `b1tninja.continuous` (it was `b1tninja.continued`), and the files are named `continuous-<platform>-2.4.2.vsix`. Another extension on the VS Code Marketplace already uses the name `continued`, so the fork needed a name of its own to be published there.

VS Code treats the new ID as a different extension:

1. Install 2.4.2.
2. Uninstall the old one: `code --uninstall-extension b1tninja.continued`.
3. Reload the window.

Your configuration carries over. API keys kept in VS Code's secure storage do not, because each extension has its own: enter them again, or keep them in `~/.continuous/.env`. The welcome screen also shows once; close it, your models are already set up.

### Names that changed

Everything that said `continue` now says `continuous`, so Continuous no longer shares names with the Continue extension and the two can be installed together:

- **The global folder is `~/.continuous`.** On first start, Continuous copies `~/.continue` there: configs, `providers.yaml`, `models.yaml`, `.env`, rules, prompts, MCP servers and sessions. The codebase index and logs are rebuilt rather than copied. `~/.continue` is not changed or removed. `CONTINUOUS_GLOBAL_DIR` sets another folder; `CONTINUE_GLOBAL_DIR` still works.
- **The workspace folder is `.continuous`.** New rules, prompts, agents, configs and plans go there. A workspace's `.continue` folder is still read, so there is nothing to move; where both have a `models.yaml` or `providers.yaml` entry with one name, `.continuous` wins.
- **`.continuousignore` and `.continuousrc.json`** replace `.continueignore` and `.continuerc.json`. The old names are still read.
- **New keys are named `CONTINUOUS_<PROVIDER>_API_KEY`** (they were `CONTINUED_…`). Configs that refer to a `CONTINUED_` name keep working; only the name suggested for a new key changed.
- **Settings, commands and views are `continuous.*`** (they were `continue.*`). On first start, every `continue.*` setting in your user and workspace settings is copied to its `continuous.*` name; the old entries are left for you to remove. Keyboard shortcuts you bound to a `continue.*` command need the new name, for example `continuous.focusContinuousInput`.

## What's new since 2.4.0

2.4.2 also includes everything in [2.4.1](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.1-vscode): a cache warning for variants with another reasoning effort, **Change model** opening the model picker, Bedrock Tab fixes for Qwen models and multi-line completions, and MCP import from Cline and Roo Code on every platform. The full list of what 2.4 brought is in the [2.4.0 release notes](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.0-vscode).

## Not included

The upstream CLI (`cn`), the JetBrains plugin and the hosted Continue Hub are not part of Continuous. Hub `uses: owner/name` blocks are not supported; configure models and blocks directly or with local file paths.
